import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv('data/credit_fraud.csv')

# Set the style of seaborn
sns.set(style="whitegrid")

# Create a figure and a set of subplots
fig, axs = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(14, 6))

# Plot 1: Distribution of transaction amounts for fraudulent vs. non-fraudulent transactions
sns.histplot(data=df, x='amount', hue='is_fraud', bins=30, kde=True, ax=axs[0], palette='coolwarm', element='step')
axs[0].set_title('Transaction Amount Distribution')
axs[0].set_xlabel('Transaction Amount')
axs[0].set_ylabel('Frequency')
axs[0].legend(title='Is Fraud', labels=['No', 'Yes'])

# Plot 2: Count of transactions by type and fraud status
sns.countplot(data=df, x='transaction_type', hue='is_fraud', ax=axs[1], palette='coolwarm')
axs[1].set_title('Transaction Type by Fraud Status')
axs[1].set_xlabel('Transaction Type')
axs[1].set_ylabel('Count')
axs[1].legend(title='Is Fraud', labels=['No', 'Yes'])

# Adjust layout
plt.tight_layout()

# Save the figure
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)

import pandas as pd

df = pd.read_csv('data/credit_fraud.csv')

# Set the style of seaborn
sns.set(style="whitegrid")

# Create a figure and a set of subplots
fig, axs = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(14, 6))

# Plot 1: Distribution of transaction amounts for fraudulent vs. non-fraudulent transactions
sns.histplot(data=df, x='amount', hue='is_fraud', bins=30, kde=True, ax=axs[0], palette='coolwarm', element='step')
axs[0].set_title('Transaction Amount Distribution')
axs[0].set_xlabel('Transaction Amount')
axs[0].set_ylabel('Frequency')
axs[0].legend(title='Is Fraud', labels=['No', 'Yes'])

# Plot 2: Count of transactions by type and fraud status
sns.countplot(data=df, x='transaction_type', hue='is_fraud', ax=axs[1], palette='coolwarm')

axs[1].set_xlabel('Transaction Type')
